title: Reading the Mechanism: Energy, Collisions and Early PCP Decisions
next: Chapter 20, Lesson 2: From mechanism to destination: triage, fluids and TXA

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already size up the scene, note the mechanism, and decide on spinal motion restriction. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Use the physics of energy to predict injuries
  2. Read a vehicle collision to find hidden injuries
  3. Turn the mechanism into PCP decisions: shock before the drop, pelvic binding

Textbook: Chapter 20, PDF pages 1669–1704
slides.say: Welcome to the trauma section. As EMRs you already look at the scene, note the mechanism of injury, or MOI, and decide whether a patient needs spinal motion restriction. As a PCP, the mechanism does more work. It tells you which injuries to look for, including the ones you can't see yet, and whether shock is coming before the blood pressure tells you. In BC, that can let you start the hypovolemia protocol early. Today: the physics of trauma, how to read a vehicle collision, and how to turn what you see into PCP decisions.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎进入创伤部分。作为 EMR，你们已经会观察现场、记下受伤机制（MOI），并判断病人是否需要脊柱活动限制。作为 PCP，受伤机制的作用更大：它告诉你该找哪些伤，包括现在还看不出来的伤，还能在血压告诉你之前，提示休克正在逼近。在 BC，这可以让你提前启动低血容量流程。今天讲：创伤的物理学、怎么读懂一场车祸，以及怎么把你看到的变成 PCP 的决定。

slides.title: Trauma is energy: speed matters most
slides.body:
Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × speed²

  • Double the weight → 2× the energy
  • Double the speed → 4× the energy
  • Head-on: speeds add; fixed object: one speed
  • Rear-end: only the difference (closing speed)
  • Body tolerates about 30 g; crashes can reach hundreds

The book's energy table mixes two formulas: trust the rule, not the table.
slides.say: Trauma is energy entering the body faster than the body can absorb it. In collisions it's kinetic energy: one half times mass times speed squared. Because speed is squared, it matters far more than weight. Double the weight and you double the energy; double the speed and you get four times the energy. In a head-on crash the two speeds add up; against a wall, one car's speed counts; in a rear-end crash, only the difference counts. The body tolerates about thirty g of deceleration, and high-speed crashes can produce hundreds. One warning: the book's energy table mixes two formulas, so learn the rule, not the table.
slides.sayZh: 创伤就是能量进入身体的速度超过了身体吸收它的能力。车祸里是动能：二分之一乘质量乘速度的平方。因为速度是平方，它比体重重要得多：体重翻倍，能量翻倍；速度翻倍，能量变成四倍。迎面相撞，两车速度相加；撞墙只算一辆车的速度；追尾只算两车的速度差。人体能承受大约三十 g 的减速，高速碰撞可以产生几百 g。提醒一句：书里的动能表混用了两个公式，记规律就好，别背表里的数字。

slides.title: Hidden injuries: blunt and deceleration
slides.body:
• Blunt: force spread out; little to see outside
  • Penetrating: force in a small area; both can occur together
  • Sudden stop → organs keep moving and tear where attached
  • Chest: the aorta is the most common deceleration injury
  • Abdomen: liver, spleen, kidneys, bowel
  • Worse head injury → more likely a neck injury too
slides.say: Blunt trauma spreads the force over a wide area, so the skin may look fine while the organs underneath are badly hurt. Penetrating trauma puts the force into a small area, and the two can happen together. The dangerous hidden injuries come from deceleration. When the body stops suddenly, the organs keep moving and tear where they're attached. In the chest, the aorta is the most common site, and a tear can be fatal within moments. In the abdomen, think liver, spleen, kidneys and bowel. And the worse the head injury, the more likely the neck is injured too. These hidden bleeds are exactly what your PCP shock assessment is hunting for.
slides.sayZh: 钝性伤把力量分散在大片区域，皮肤可能看着没事，下面的器官却伤得很重。穿透伤把力量集中在一小块，两者可以同时发生。危险的隐匿伤来自减速：身体突然停住，器官继续往前冲，在固定的地方撕裂。胸部最常见的是主动脉，一旦撕裂可能很快致命。腹部要想到肝、脾、肾和肠。而且头伤越重，颈部同时受伤的可能越大。这些看不见的出血，正是你作为 PCP 评估休克时要找的。

slides.title: Five collisions in every crash
slides.body:
Vehicle stops→Occupant stops→Organs stop
Loose objects and people hit→Extra impacts

Each phase adds injury. A frontal crash that hurts the hip, then a side hit, can add a pelvic injury.
slides.say: The textbook describes every crash as five collisions in a row. First, the vehicle hits something and stops. Second, the occupant stops, against a seat belt, an airbag, or the wheel and windshield. Third, the organs stop, slamming into the skull, the ribs and their attachments. Fourth, secondary impacts: loose objects, pets or other passengers keep flying at the original speed and hit someone who has already stopped. Fifth, additional impacts, when the vehicle is pushed into something else. Each phase can add injuries. A frontal crash that hurts the hip, followed by a side hit, can add a pelvic injury. So always ask: how many times was this patient hit?
slides.sayZh: 教材把每一场车祸描述成连续的五次碰撞。第一，车撞上东西停下。第二，人停下，撞在安全带、气囊，或方向盘和挡风玻璃上。第三，器官停下，撞向颅骨、肋骨和它们的固定结构。第四，二次撞击：车里没固定的东西、宠物或其他乘客以原速继续飞来，砸在已经停下的人身上。第五，附加撞击：车又被推去撞别的东西。每一阶段都可能增加伤情。正面撞伤了髋部，再被侧面一撞，就可能再加上骨盆损伤。所以一定要问：这个病人被撞了几次？

slides.title: Frontal impact: two pathways
slides.body:
PathwayLeads withLook for
Down and underknees into the dashknee, femur, hip dislocation, pelvis
Up and overhead into windshieldhead, neck, larynx; ejection
  • Bent steering wheel → critical driver injury until proven otherwise
  • Cracked windshield → neck injury until proven otherwise
  • Chest into the wheel: ribs, lungs, heart, aorta
slides.say: In a frontal crash, unrestrained occupants follow one of two paths. Down and under: the knees hit the dashboard and the force travels up the femurs, so look for knee injuries, femur fractures, hip dislocations and pelvic fractures. Up and over: the head hits the windshield or roof, so look for head and neck injuries, a crushed larynx from the wheel, or ejection. Two rules from the textbook: a bent steering wheel means a critical driver injury until proven otherwise, and a cracked windshield means a neck injury until proven otherwise. When the chest hits the wheel, think ribs, lungs, heart and aorta.
slides.sayZh: 正面碰撞时，没系安全带的乘员会走两条路径之一。下潜路径：膝盖撞仪表台，力量沿股骨往上传，要找膝部损伤、股骨骨折、髋关节脱位和骨盆骨折。上越路径：头撞挡风玻璃或车顶，要找头颈部损伤、方向盘撞碎喉部，或被抛出车外。教材的两条规则：方向盘变形，司机就有致命伤，直到排除为止；挡风玻璃裂了，就有颈部损伤，直到排除为止。胸口撞上方向盘，要想到肋骨、肺、心脏和主动脉。

slides.q: An unrestrained driver hit a pole head-on. The steering wheel is bent and there's a dent under the dash at knee level. He's talking; BP 128/80, HR 104. What's your best working picture?
options: He's talking with a normal BP, so his injuries are minor
Suspect chest injury from the wheel and knee, femur, hip and pelvic injury from the dash: treat as critical
Only his knees hit, so assess and splint the legs
Expect only a whiplash injury of the neck
slides.say: Let's use that. An unrestrained driver hit a pole head-on. The steering wheel is bent, and there's a dent under the dash at knee level. He's talking. Blood pressure one hundred twenty-eight over eighty, heart rate one hundred four. What's your best working picture? A, he's talking with a normal blood pressure, so his injuries are minor. B, suspect chest injury from the wheel, and knee, femur, hip and pelvic injury from the dash, and treat him as critical. C, only his knees hit, so assess and splint the legs. D, expect only a whiplash injury of the neck. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来用一下。一名没系安全带的司机正面撞上电线杆，方向盘变形，仪表台下方膝盖高度有一处凹痕。他能说话，血压一百二十八/八十，心率一百零四。你最合理的初步判断是什么？A 能说话、血压正常，伤不重；B 怀疑方向盘造成胸部伤、仪表台造成膝、股骨、髋和骨盆伤，按危重处理；C 只有膝盖撞了，评估并固定双腿就行；D 只考虑颈部挥鞭伤。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A bent steering wheel means a critical driver injury until proven otherwise, and a knee dent points to the down-and-under pathway: knee, femur, hip and pelvis. A is the classic trap: a talking patient with a normal blood pressure can still be compensating for a hidden bleed, and his heart rate is already up. C ignores the chest. D describes a rear-end mechanism, not a frontal one.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。方向盘变形意味着司机有致命伤，直到排除为止；膝盖凹痕提示下潜路径：膝、股骨、髋和骨盆。A 是典型陷阱：能说话、血压正常的病人，仍可能在代偿隐匿出血，而且他的心率已经升高了。C 忽略了胸部。D 说的是追尾的机制，不是正面碰撞。

slides.title: Side, rear, spin and rollover
slides.body:
• Side: near-side chest and pelvis; belts help little
  • Look for ribs, lungs, diaphragm, clavicle, pelvic ring
  • Rear: whiplash; headrest behind the head, not the neck
  • Rotational: a mix of frontal and side injuries
  • Rollover: most lethal; ejection raises death risk 2–25×
  • About 1 in 3 ejected occupants has a neck fracture
slides.say: Now the other impact types. In a side, or T-bone, crash, the force goes straight into the near-side occupant's chest and pelvis, and the seat belt helps little because it's built to stop forward motion. Look for rib fractures, bruised lungs, a torn diaphragm, a broken clavicle, and a lateral compression fracture of the pelvic ring. Rear impacts cause whiplash; the headrest should sit behind the head, not the neck. A rotational crash gives a mix of frontal and side injuries. Rollovers have the greatest potential to kill, even with belts on. Ejection raises the risk of death two to twenty-five times, and about one in three ejected occupants has a neck fracture.
slides.sayZh: 再看其他撞击方式。侧面撞击，也叫 T 字撞，力量直接打在靠撞击侧乘员的胸部和骨盆上，安全带帮助不大，因为它是为防止向前冲设计的。要找肋骨骨折、肺挫伤、膈肌破裂、锁骨骨折，以及骨盆环的外侧压缩型骨折。追尾会造成挥鞭伤，头枕应该在头后面，而不是颈后面。旋转撞击是正面伤和侧面伤的混合。翻滚致命的可能最大，系了安全带也一样。被抛出车外，死亡风险增加二到二十五倍，大约三分之一被抛出的人有颈椎骨折。

slides.title: Belts, airbags and higher-risk patients
slides.body:
• Seat belts: about 45% fewer deaths; frontal airbags: about 30%
  • Lap belt worn too high → abdominal and lumbar injuries
  • Older adults: even a fall from standing can break ribs, hip, spine
  • Blood thinners: a minor head bump can bleed badly
  • Child too big for a car seat, no booster → abdominal injury
  • Pregnancy: lap and shoulder belt protect mother and baby
slides.say: Restraints change the injuries you'll find. Seat belts cut deaths by about forty-five percent, and airbags cut deaths in direct frontal crashes by about thirty percent. But a lap belt worn across the belly instead of low on the pelvis can cause abdominal and lumbar spine injuries. Some patients are hurt worse by the same mechanism. In older adults, even a fall from standing can break ribs, a hip or the spine. Patients on blood thinners can bleed badly after a minor head bump, so always ask about medications. A child who has outgrown a car seat but has no booster risks abdominal injury. And in pregnancy, a lap belt plus a shoulder belt protects mother and baby.
slides.sayZh: 约束装置会改变你看到的伤。安全带让死亡减少约百分之四十五，气囊让正面直撞的死亡减少约百分之三十。但腰带如果系在肚子上而不是低低压在骨盆上，就可能造成腹部和腰椎损伤。同样的机制，有些病人伤得更重。老年人连站立时跌倒都可能摔断肋骨、髋部或脊柱。服抗凝药的人轻轻撞到头也可能严重出血，所以一定要问用药。孩子已经超出儿童座椅、却没用增高座椅，有腹部损伤风险。孕妇要腰带加肩带一起系，才能同时保护母亲和胎儿。

slides.title: Shock before the BP drops
slides.body:
BC Hypovolemia protocol, footnote 2

May be used with systolic over 90 if shock is expected

  • Expected from the mechanism, the injuries, or the patient's condition
  • PCP: vascular access en route, or on scene only if delayed
  • Bolus 20 mL/kg (max 2 L) for hypoperfusion or hypotension
  • Reassess every 500 mL; consider TXA for shock from blood loss
slides.say: Here the mechanism becomes a PCP decision. The BC hypovolemia protocol normally needs a systolic under ninety plus signs of shock. But footnote two says you may use it with a pressure above ninety if shock is expected because of the mechanism of injury, the nature and extent of the injuries, or the patient's condition. Picture an ejected rollover patient who is talking, with a pressure of one hundred twenty and a pulse of one hundred fifteen. You don't wait for the crash. You get vascular access en route, or on scene only if there's a delay. But starting early isn't flooding early: give a bolus only to correct hypoperfusion or hypotension, reassess every five hundred millilitres, and consider TXA.
slides.sayZh: 这里，受伤机制变成了 PCP 的决定。BC 低血容量流程通常要求收缩压低于九十并有休克征象。但脚注二说，如果因为受伤机制、损伤的性质和范围，或病人的状况，预计会发生休克，血压高于九十也可以启动。想象一个翻滚被抛出车外的病人，还能说话，血压一百二十，脉搏一百一十五。你不用等他垮掉：在转运途中建立静脉通路，只有现场有延误时才在现场做。但提早启动不等于提早大量补液：只有为了纠正灌注不足或低血压才给液体，每五百毫升复评一次，并考虑 TXA。

slides.title: Mechanisms that break the pelvis
slides.body:
• Side impact on the patient's side (pelvic ring)
  • Knees into the dash: force up the femurs
  • A second impact after a frontal crash

BC: bind before transport if a major mechanism plus any of:

  • HR > 100 or systolic < 90; pelvic pain or instability
  • Decreased LOC, or a major injury distracting from the exam

Not for hip (neck-of-femur) fractures or simple falls from standing.
slides.say: Pelvic fractures can bleed heavily and hide it. Today's mechanisms that point to the pelvis: a side impact on the patient's side, knees driven into the dashboard, and a second impact after the first crash. Every licence level binds the pelvis, but the decision starts with the mechanism. In BC, bind before transport when a major mechanism suggests a pelvic fracture, plus any one of these: a heart rate over one hundred or a systolic under ninety, pelvic pain or instability, a decreased level of consciousness, or another major injury distracting from the exam. Don't bind a hip fracture, meaning a broken neck of the femur, or a simple fall from standing.
slides.sayZh: 骨盆骨折可以大量出血，而且藏得很深。今天讲的指向骨盆的机制：撞在病人这一侧的侧面撞击、膝盖撞进仪表台，以及第一次碰撞后的第二次撞击。所有级别都会固定骨盆，但决定要从受伤机制开始。在 BC，只要有提示骨盆骨折的重大机制，再加上以下任意一项，就要在转运前固定骨盆：心率超过一百或收缩压低于九十、骨盆疼痛或不稳定、意识水平下降，或有其他重伤干扰骨盆检查。髋部骨折，也就是股骨颈骨折，以及站立高度的简单跌倒，不用骨盆带。

slides.q: A restrained driver was T-boned on her side. She's anxious; HR 118, BP 112/74, and pressing on her pelvis hurts. You're the PCP. What's the best plan?
options: Her systolic is over 90, so the hypovolemia protocol doesn't apply yet
Bind the pelvis, start transport, and run the hypovolemia protocol en route: IV, consider a bolus and TXA
Start an IV and give 2 L on scene before you move her
Skip the binder: she was wearing a seat belt
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A restrained driver was T-boned on her side. She's anxious, her heart rate is one hundred eighteen, her blood pressure is one hundred twelve over seventy-four, and pressing on her pelvis hurts. You're the PCP. What's the best plan? A, her systolic is over ninety, so the hypovolemia protocol doesn't apply yet. B, bind the pelvis, start transport, and run the hypovolemia protocol en route: IV access, and consider a bolus and TXA. C, start an IV and give two litres on scene before you move her. D, skip the binder, because she was wearing a seat belt. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名系了安全带的女司机在她这一侧被 T 字撞。她很焦虑，心率一百一十八，血压一百一十二/七十四，按压骨盆会痛。你是 PCP，最好的方案是什么？A 收缩压高于九十，所以低血容量流程还不适用；B 固定骨盆、出发，在途中执行低血容量流程：建立静脉通路，考虑补液和 TXA；C 先在现场开静脉、输两升再搬动她；D 她系了安全带，不用骨盆带。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A side impact on her side is a major mechanism, and pelvic pain plus a heart rate over one hundred meets BC's binding rules. Her anxiety and fast pulse suggest compensated shock, and BC lets you start the hypovolemia protocol above ninety when shock is expected. A ignores that footnote. C keeps her on scene and skips the five-hundred-millilitre reassessments. D is wrong because seat belts do little in side impacts.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。撞在她这一侧的侧面撞击是重大机制，骨盆疼痛加上心率超过一百，符合 BC 的骨盆固定标准。她的焦虑和快速脉搏提示代偿期休克，而 BC 允许在预计会休克时，收缩压高于九十也启动低血容量流程。A 忽略了这条脚注。C 把她留在现场，也跳过了每五百毫升的复评。D 错在安全带对侧面撞击帮助很小。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: a mechanism that predicts shock
slides.body:
BC Hypovolemia protocol and Pelvis binding

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Control external bleeding
  • Bind the pelvis before transport, if indicated
  • Splint fractures; lay the patient supine
  • Keep warm; oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%

PCP adds (en route or if delayed)

  • Vascular access
  • Bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  • Consider TXA: shock from blood loss or hidden bleeding

Shock expected from the mechanism? The protocol may start with systolic > 90.
slides.say: Here's how the two licences divide the work when the mechanism predicts bleeding. On the left, everything you already do as an EMR: control external bleeding, bind the pelvis before transport when the rules say so, splint fractures, lay the patient flat, keep them warm, and give oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher. On the right, what the PCP adds, en route or if there's a delay: vascular access, a fluid bolus of twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred, and TXA when shock comes from blood loss or hidden bleeding. And remember the footnote: you can start before the pressure falls.
slides.sayZh: 当受伤机制提示会出血时，两种执照这样分工。左边是你作为 EMR 本来就做的：控制外出血；符合标准时在转运前固定骨盆；固定骨折；让病人平卧；保暖；给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上。右边是 PCP 增加的，在途中或现场有延误时做：建立静脉通路；按每公斤二十毫升补液、最多两升、每五百毫升复评；休克源于失血或隐匿出血时考虑 TXA。别忘了那条脚注：可以在血压下降之前就启动。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• After a big mechanism, a normal BP does not rule out shock
  • The IV goes in en route; never a longer scene time
  • Mechanism alone isn't a reason for a bolus: treat perfusion
  • Don't bind a hip fracture or a simple fall from standing
  • Lap-belt mark across the belly: think bowel and lumbar spine
  • Blood thinners + any head bump = high risk, even if well
slides.say: Now the new watch-outs. One: after a big mechanism, a normal blood pressure doesn't rule out shock; the heart rate, skin and mental status tell you more. Two: the IV goes in en route. The mechanism can justify early access, but never a longer scene time. Three: the mechanism alone isn't a reason for a bolus; give fluid to correct hypoperfusion or hypotension, then reassess. Four: don't bind a hip fracture or a simple fall from standing. Five: a lap-belt mark across the belly means think bowel and lumbar spine. And six: a patient on blood thinners with even a minor head bump is high risk, even if they look well.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲新的注意事项。一，重大机制之后，血压正常不能排除休克，心率、皮肤和神志告诉你的更多。二，静脉通路在途中建立；受伤机制可以让你提早开通路，但绝不能因此延长现场时间。三，单凭机制不是补液的理由；补液是为了纠正灌注不足或低血压，补完要复评。四，髋部骨折或站立跌倒不用骨盆带。五，腹部有横过的腰带勒痕，要想到肠和腰椎。六，服抗凝药的人哪怕只是轻轻撞到头，也属高危，即使看起来很好。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Hypovolemia protocol: may start with systolic > 90 if shock is expected
  • Pelvic binder: not for hip fractures or simple falls from standing
  • Hip dislocation (knees into dash) → Rapid Transport Category
  • Hip reduces on its own → update the receiving hospital
  • Book: rib injuries may need decompression → BC exam: no needle decompression
slides.say: Now the BC points that link to today's mechanisms. First, the hypovolemia protocol may start with a systolic above ninety when shock is expected. Second, the pelvic binder is not for hip fractures or simple falls from standing. Third, the down-and-under pathway can dislocate a hip, and in BC every hip dislocation is in the Rapid Transport Category: a critical patient for rapid transport. If the hip reduces on its own during care or transport, update the receiving hospital. Fourth, the book says broken ribs can let air into the chest that needs decompression. The BC chest trauma protocol on the licensing exam has no needle decompression, and in BCEHS it's an ACP skill. Seal an open chest wound, and lift a corner if tension develops.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲和今天这些机制相关的 BC 要点。第一，预计会休克时，收缩压高于九十也可以启动低血容量流程。第二，骨盆带不用于髋部骨折，也不用于站立高度的简单跌倒。第三，下潜路径可能造成髋关节脱位，而在 BC，所有髋关节脱位都属于快速转运类别（RTC），即需要快速转运的危重病人。如果在处置或转运中髋关节自行复位，要告知接收医院。第四，书里说肋骨骨折可能让空气进入胸腔、需要减压。BC 执照考试的胸部创伤流程里没有针刺减压（在 BCEHS 它属于 ACP 技能）；开放性胸伤用封闭敷料封住，出现张力征象时掀开一角。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Speed is squared: double the speed, four times the energy
  2. Read the wreck: bent wheel = critical driver; knee dent = femur, hip, pelvis
  3. Mechanism → PCP decisions: hypovolemia care before the drop; bind when BC says so

Next: motorcycles, falls, weapons and blasts; where to go; fluids and TXA
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: speed is squared, so double the speed means four times the energy. Two: read the wreck. A bent steering wheel means a critical driver until proven otherwise, a knee dent means femur, hip and pelvis, and a side impact means chest and pelvis on the near side. Three: turn the mechanism into PCP decisions. When shock is expected, BC lets you start the hypovolemia protocol before the pressure falls, with the IV en route, and you bind the pelvis when the BC criteria are met. Next lesson: motorcycles, pedestrians, falls, weapons and blasts, where to take the patient, and how to use fluids and TXA. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，速度是平方：速度翻倍，能量变成四倍。二，读懂事故现场：方向盘变形就是危重司机，直到排除为止；膝盖凹痕指向股骨、髋和骨盆；侧面撞击指向撞击侧的胸部和骨盆。三，把机制变成 PCP 的决定：预计会休克时，BC 允许在血压下降前启动低血容量流程，静脉通路在途中建立；符合 BC 标准时固定骨盆。下节课讲摩托车、行人、坠落、刀枪伤和爆炸伤，病人该送去哪里，以及怎么用补液和 TXA。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
